q.t: Which instrument draws circles and arcs?
q.e: Its fixed opening keeps the pencil the same distance from the needle point.

q.t: Which instrument measures the length of a line segment?
q.e: A ruler is marked in centimetres and millimetres.

q.t: Which instrument measures angles?
q.e: It is marked in degrees.

q.t: A line that cuts a segment into two equal parts at 90° is its:
q.e: Perpendicular = at right angles; bisector = cuts in half.

q.t: With a compass alone, the easiest angle to construct is:
q.e: Marking the radius on an arc makes an equilateral triangle, whose angles are 60°.

q.t: Bisecting a 90° angle gives an angle of:
q.e: Bisect means halve.

q.t: To draw a circle of radius 3 cm, the compass must be opened to:
q.e: The compass opening is the radius — the distance from centre to circle.

q.t: A perpendicular meets a line at an angle of:
q.e: Perpendicular means at right angles.

q.t: To copy a line segment exactly, without measuring, we use a:
q.e: Open the compass to the segment’s length and mark the same length on a new line.

q.t: The bisector of an angle divides it into:
q.e: ‘Bi’ means two and ‘sect’ means cut.

q.t: Bisecting a 60° angle gives:
q.e: Half of 60°.

q.t: Marking the radius twice along an arc from the base line gives an angle of:
q.e: Each step of the radius along the arc is 60°.

q.t: A 90° angle can be constructed by bisecting the angle between:
q.e: 90° is exactly halfway between 60° and 120°.

q.t: Which angle is obtained by bisecting a right angle?
q.e: Half of 90°.

q.t: A 135° angle is made up of:
q.e: 90 + 45 = 135. Both can be made with ruler and compass.

q.t: Bisecting a 30° angle gives:
q.e: Half of 30°.

q.t: The perpendicular bisector of an 8 cm segment crosses it how far from each end (in cm)?
q.e: It passes through the midpoint.

q.t: Any point on the perpendicular bisector of segment AB is:
o: The same distance from A and from B
q.e: The bisector is the mirror line between A and B, so everything on it is equally far from both.

q.t: Bisecting a 70° angle gives:
q.e: Half of 70°.

q.t: How many perpendiculars can be drawn to a line from a point outside it?
q.e: Only one line through the point meets the given line at exactly 90° — the shortest path to it.

q.t: A 75° angle is made up of:
q.e: 60 + 15 = 75, and 15° comes from bisecting 30°.

q.t: A 105° angle is made up of:
A right angle is bisected, and one of the halves is bisected again. Find the size of the smallest angle (in degrees).
A 150° angle can be made by taking 30° away from:
q.e: 150 = 180 − 30: construct 30° at the other end of a straight line.

q.t: Bisecting a straight angle gives:
q.e: Half of 180° — this is how a perpendicular is constructed.

q.t: A 7.4 cm segment is bisected. How long is each part (in cm)?
q.e: Half of 7.4.

q.t: To construct the perpendicular bisector of AB, the arcs are drawn from:
o: Both A and B, with the same radius
q.e: Equal arcs from both ends cross at points equally far from A and B, which lie on the bisector.

q.t: Any point on the bisector of an angle is:
o: The same distance from both arms
q.e: The bisector is the mirror line of the angle.

q.t: Which of these angles can NOT be made by starting from 60° or 90° and bisecting?
q.e: Halving 60 gives 30, 15, 7.5 … and halving 90 gives 45, 22.5 … 20° never appears.

q.t: Bisecting a 75° angle gives:
q.e: Half of 75°.

q.t: A 67.5° angle is made up of 45° and:
q.e: 67.5 − 45 = 22.5, which is half of 45°.

q.t: How many times must a 60° angle be bisected, one after another, to get 7.5°?
q.e: 60 → 30 → 15 → 7.5: three bisections.

q.t: A 10 cm segment is bisected, and each half is bisected again. How long is each small part (in cm)?
q.e: 10 → 5 → 2.5: four equal parts.

q.t: A 165° angle can be made by taking away from 180° an angle of:
Bisecting a 105° angle gives:
q.e: Half of 105°.

q.t: To bisect a 12 cm segment, the compass opening must be:
q.e: The arcs from the two ends must cross. With 6 cm or less they would only touch or miss.

q.t: Two angles on a straight line are bisected. What is the angle between the two bisectors (in degrees)?
q.e: The two angles total 180°, so their halves total 90°.

q.t: A 96° angle is bisected three times in a row. Find the final angle (in degrees).
The perpendicular bisectors of two chords of a circle meet at:
q.e: Every point on a chord’s perpendicular bisector is equally far from its ends — and the centre is equally far from all points of the circle.

q.t: An angle is bisected twice and the result is 18°. What was the original angle (in degrees)?
q.e: Undo the two halvings: 18 × 2 × 2 = 72.
